tasks.short: Advise managers on collective agreements, employee discipline, and grievance procedures.

steps.what: Receive the manager's question and establish the immediate deadline.
Retrieve the relevant agreement, policy, and restricted case history.
Check procedural stages, notice periods, and missing mandatory records.
Prepare advice options and questions requiring clarification.

loop.input: Approved agreement and policy extracts, restricted case facts, and procedure check.
loop.output: Source-linked advice options, missing facts, and escalation questions.
loop.check: Specialist verifies jurisdiction, source currency, factual distinctions, and every proposed action.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing authority or conflicting sources trigger manual advice.
loop.why_not_simpler: Manager questions and case narratives vary; templates alone cannot connect the relevant passages.

steps.what: Judge fairness, proportionality, precedent, and the need for legal escalation.
Discuss the recommendation and coach the manager through the next conversation.
Record advice, responsibilities, and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: A restricted register in {WORKFLOW} links advice requests to current sources in {DOCS} and authorised records in {HCM}. Deterministic checklists calculate procedural dates, while a bounded loop drafts source-linked options for specialist review. Approved next steps populate the case record and {CALENDAR}; managers retain responsibility for employment actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depended on scattered case histories, local interpretations, and sensitive facts that generic knowledge bases could not safely resolve.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled source collections, permission-aware retrieval, and explicit procedure tables can support useful preparation. Small model loops can draft from that evidence without deciding disciplinary outcomes.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, fairness, incomplete accounts, and conflicting obligations require specialist judgement. GDPR and national employment rules apply; any extension into worker evaluation needs a separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge a manager's framing, hear the employee's perspective, and identify when an apparently compliant action would be unfair.

ambition.what: A monthly grievance prevention clinic for first-line managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time coaching managers and spotting recurring procedural failures. They can initiate preventive coaching within their remit; disciplinary and appeal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Review whether recurring grievances require a policy change.
reach.learn: Policy governance, employee consultation, and how to distinguish isolated incidents from systemic problems.

evidence.claim: Case registers, procedural date rules, and scheduled reminders are established deterministic patterns.
Source-linked draft advice can reduce preparation, but the digest provides no validated labor-relations advice case.

assumptions: Time shares describe a substantive advice case; simple factual questions take a different route.
The relevant procedure and jurisdiction are selected by a specialist before date rules run.
Confidential advice records remain separate from broadly visible employee records.
Automated record updates use structured next steps entered during the human conversation.
Build ranges cover one procedure family and allow national consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Where are grievance and disciplinary records stored, and who may access them?
Which advice requires legal counsel or HR manager approval?
Which national rules and collective agreements determine deadlines?
What retention, legal-hold, and employee-access rules apply?
research_questions: Can permission checks prevent retrieval across unrelated employee cases?
How reliably do procedure rules handle pauses, appeals, and disputed receipt dates?
Which request types can be answered entirely from approved factual guidance?
new_work: Review draft advice and resolve conflicting or outdated sources.
Maintain procedure tables and source effective dates.
Check access controls and restricted case links.
Review recurring process issues without exposing identifiable complaint details.
tasks.statement: Advise management on matters related to the administration of contracts or employee discipline or grievance procedures.

tasks.short: Meet interested parties to discuss negotiations, grievances and other labor relations matters.

steps.what: Review the matter, relevant clauses and previous correspondence.

loop.input: Authorised case documents and correspondence.
loop.output: Case brief separating recorded facts, allegations, positions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Specialist verifies chronology, references, representation rights and omitted counter-evidence.
loop.stop: One summary and one correction pass; contradictions remain explicit for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text correspondence contains conflicting accounts that fixed fields cannot summarise adequately.

steps.what: Arrange participants, availability and practical meeting requirements.
Prepare the agenda, evidence pack and mandate reminders.
Hear concerns, clarify positions and explore possible resolutions within the mandate.
Approve proposed commitments that exceed the specialist's existing mandate.
Prepare and circulate the checked meeting record, positions and next actions.

loop.input: Specialist's written notes and approved positions.
loop.output: Meeting record distinguishing agreed points, proposals, disagreements and assigned actions.
loop.check: Specialist verifies wording and disclosure scope before circulation; disputed points remain marked.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unclear commitments require human clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Written notes require contextual phrasing to avoid presenting tentative proposals as agreements.

tasks.design: Configured {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL} flows arrange meetings using approved participants and neutral invitations. A bounded model prepares a referenced case brief in {DOCS}; deterministic templates assemble the meeting pack, and a second bounded drafting step prepares minutes from written notes. People conduct the conversation, approve concessions and check every circulated record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sensitive conversations depend on trust, representation and context. Preparation and records were often bundled with the meeting itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features and simple document assembly cover routine coordination. Bounded reading and drafting can reduce preparation work without replacing the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Contested facts, accessibility needs, representation rights and careful wording of commitments remain demanding. Participants may disagree about the meeting record.
tasks.human_edge: Listening, building trust, managing conflict and knowing when to pause or seek a different resolution.

ambition.what: Offer an early facilitated conversation before a concern becomes a formal grievance.

tasks.altitude: More of the specialist's week becomes available for direct conversations and follow-up. They can offer earlier intervention within existing authority; settlement rights do not automatically expand.

reach.task: Identify when a grievance needs a specialist discrimination response.
reach.learn: Protected grounds, impartial intake, reasonable adjustments and escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Scheduling and document assembly are feasible support tools; bargaining and grievance conversations remain human work.
The EU AI Act prohibits workplace emotion recognition, subject to its specified exceptions.
Source checking matters when generated text could introduce unsupported statements.

assumptions: The steps represent a typical substantive meeting; approval is needed only when proposals exceed the mandate.
Routine scheduling uses an approved participant list and reveals no grievance details in invitations.
The design uses written notes and does not require recording or emotion analysis.
The supplied low automation prior fits the conversation itself; preparation and paperwork offer a larger gain.
unknowns: Who may attend, represent a party or approve commitments.
Which cases require separate investigation or legal involvement.
Existing rules for sharing records and correcting disputed minutes.
Language, interpretation and accessibility requirements.
research_questions: Which preparation documents can be reused without exposing another case's information?
Can participants distinguish proposals from agreements in the generated meeting record?
What GDPR and national rules govern case access, representative information and retention?
new_work: Check briefs for missing counter-evidence and incorrect chronology.
Review disclosure scope before sharing packs or minutes.
Resolve participant corrections and disputed records.
Maintain invitation templates, participant permissions and agenda templates.
tasks.statement: Call or meet with union, company, government, or other interested parties to discuss labor relations matters, such as contract negotiations or grievances.

tasks.short: Draft bargaining proposals and counterproposals from approved terms.

steps.what: Select the authoritative agreement, approved resolution and drafting instructions.
Write proposed clauses and counterproposal wording.

loop.input: Version-locked drafting pack, approved clause library and proposal template.
loop.output: Clause draft with a source map and unresolved choices marked.
loop.check: Compare every commitment to approved instructions; reuse approved wording verbatim where applicable.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unresolved intent goes back to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing clauses can be assembled deterministically, but novel counterproposal wording needs contextual drafting.

steps.what: Compare versions and check dates, amounts, definitions and cross-references.
Review legal meaning, enforceability and unintended changes.
Approve the proposal for release against the negotiating mandate.
Send the approved version and record its release.

tasks.design: A generator assembles approved clauses and instructions from the {CLM} and {DOCS}, using a bounded drafting loop only for new wording. Deterministic comparison checks produce a change report, and the {WORKFLOW} releases the approved version through the {EMAIL} after recipient confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved intentions are expressed in narrative instructions, while clause dependencies and version control require careful manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Document assembly, comparison and controlled release are established techniques. Bounded drafting can handle novel wording while retaining source maps and human legal review.
tasks.still_hard: A small wording change can alter obligations across several clauses. Legal interpretation, multilingual equivalence and missing negotiating intent remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Translate negotiated intent into precise obligations and recognise wording that creates an unintended concession.

ambition.what: Clause-level implementation impact note for each proposed agreement change.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time producing first drafts and comparisons, and more time checking intent and implementation consequences. Authority to approve or release proposals does not expand automatically.

reach.task: Translate changed agreement clauses into employee guidance and operating procedures.
reach.learn: Clause interpretation, effective-date transitions and clear explanations of employee entitlements.

evidence.claim: Clause assembly, document comparison and controlled release can use deterministic technology; contextual drafting needs review.
The digest documents fabricated references in a generated report, supporting source checks before external release.

assumptions: The task starts with approved negotiating intent; choosing concessions is counted in resolution design and bargaining.
The proposed automation prepares text and checks structure; it does not certify legal validity.
Time shares give drafting more weight than meetings because the task boundary excludes formal negotiation.
Source selection and legal review may remain substantial even when first-draft production is faster.
Access work covers confidential material, GDPR requirements where personal data appears, EU AI Act intended use and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Is there a maintained clause library with authoritative versions?
Which languages and agreement formats are required?
Who approves wording and who may release it?
Can existing document tools produce reliable comparisons and immutable release records?
research_questions: Which recurring proposals can be generated entirely from approved clauses and structured fields?
Can checks detect changed amounts, broken references and unintended omissions in representative historical drafts?
new_work: Maintain approved clauses, templates and their effective dates.
Review novel wording and unresolved intent.
Investigate failed comparison checks and clause dependencies.
Maintain release permissions, recipient lists and source-version records.
tasks.statement: Draft contract proposals or counter-proposals for collective bargaining or other labor negotiations.

tasks.short: Draft and agree procedures governing collective bargaining with employer and employee representatives.

steps.what: Collect existing procedures, agreements and relevant legal guidance.
Agree drafting scope, representation, meeting rules and unresolved process questions.
Draft procedure clauses and mark departures from the existing text.

loop.input: Approved clause library, procedure requirements and current procedure.
loop.output: Procedure draft with changes, source references and open points.
loop.check: Check required sections and cross-references; specialist verifies meaning and flags unsupported clauses.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision passes per version; unresolved clauses return to human discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreed requirements require contextual wording, although standard clauses and document structure remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss disputed clauses and agree revisions with employer and employee representatives.
Check the revised procedure against applicable law and existing agreements.
Approve the final wording through the agreed representative process.
Publish the approved procedure and archive superseded versions.

tasks.design: A versioned clause library in {DOCS} supplies standard wording, while a bounded loop drafts only from agreed requirements and approved sources. {WORKFLOW} routes legal review and representative approval, then publishes the approved version in {DOCS} and sends an internal notice through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated drafting and version control sit around a process whose substance must be negotiated. Standard templates cover only part of the wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Document versioning and approval routing already exist. Bounded drafting can turn agreed requirements into a reviewable text without automating agreement between the parties.
tasks.still_hard: Representation rights, enforceability and ambiguous wording depend on national rules and the applicable agreements. A specialist cannot create government regulations merely by publishing a company procedure.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing a process that representatives regard as legitimate, especially when their interests conflict.

ambition.what: Joint procedure walkthrough for newly appointed employee representatives.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time managing versions and more time explaining disputed clauses and improving the bargaining process. Legal approval and representative authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Create an induction session on the agreed bargaining procedure.
reach.learn: Learning objectives, realistic exercises and checking procedural understanding.

reach.task: Maintain the authoritative procedure register.
reach.learn: Version control, effective dates and retention requirements.

evidence.claim: Clause assembly, version control and approval routing are established automation patterns.
Bargaining remains human work, with drafting open to bounded assistance.
In the Netherlands, specified HR data and monitoring arrangements require works-council consent.
A documented report failure supports verifying generated references before legal review.

assumptions: The typical employer drafts bargaining procedures rather than statutory regulations.
Employer and employee representatives retain their separate approval rights.
Time shares cover one drafting cycle; repeated negotiation rounds can increase the conversation share.
The priors favour drafting support, while the steps retain substantive consultation and legal review.
Build estimates cover a pilot and applicable employee consultation; bargaining delays are excluded.
unknowns: Which representative bodies and signatories must approve the procedure.
Applicable national rules and existing sector or company agreements.
Whether there is an approved clause library.
Which publication channels make the procedure authoritative.
Whether drafting materials contain personal or special-category data.
research_questions: Which clauses can be assembled unchanged from approved templates?
Can existing document approvals preserve each representative body's separate decision?
new_work: Review generated clauses and reconcile agreed revisions.
Maintain the approved clause library and legal source dates.
Resolve approval exceptions and conflicting versions.
Check that notices and training refer to the effective procedure.
tasks.statement: Draft rules or regulations to govern collective bargaining activities in collaboration with company, government, or employee representatives.

tasks.short: Develop and assess workable alternatives to proposals raised in labour negotiations.

steps.what: Read the proposal against the current agreement and identify requested changes.

loop.input: Proposal and current collective agreement.
loop.output: Clause comparison with requested changes and missing details.
loop.check: Link changes to exact passages; specialist checks exceptions, definitions and omissions.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass; unmatched clauses remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals often describe changes indirectly and use different wording from the agreement.

steps.what: Clarify interests, constraints and acceptable trade-offs with the relevant representatives.
Calculate costs and affected employee groups for candidate alternatives.
Develop alternative packages and describe their practical trade-offs.

loop.input: Reviewed constraints, verified cost scenarios and sourced legal research.
loop.output: Alternative packages with explicit trade-offs and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Use calculated costs unchanged; specialist checks feasibility, legal concerns and alignment with stated interests.
loop.stop: At most three packages and one correction pass; infeasible options are discarded.
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining interests into usable packages needs variable prose and contextual reasoning beyond a scenario calculator.

steps.what: Select the recommended package and authorise its use in negotiations.
Assemble the approved options brief for the negotiating team.

tasks.design: A deterministic scenario calculator uses authorised data from {HCM} and {PAYROLL} to compare costs and employee groups. Bounded loops compare proposal text and draft alternatives in {DOCS}; human discussions establish interests, and {WORKFLOW} records the HR manager's approval before producing the negotiating brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost models and proposal documents are disconnected. Acceptable trade-offs depend on relationships and interests that are rarely written down.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation rules and document assembly are established technology. Bounded extraction and drafting can connect varied proposals to those tools with less custom development.
tasks.still_hard: Affordability does not establish acceptability. Distributional effects, national employment rules and representatives' willingness to compromise remain judgement calls.
tasks.human_edge: Finding an exchange that both sides can defend to their constituents.

ambition.what: Reassess costed bargaining packages between negotiation rounds.

tasks.altitude: The specialist can bring several checked packages to each round and spend more time testing their acceptability. Approval of employer commitments remains with the authorised decision maker.

reach.task: Assess the distributional effect of a proposed pay settlement.
reach.learn: Pay components, workforce segmentation and recurring versus one-off costs.

reach.task: Check whether proposed pay rules can be implemented.
reach.learn: Effective dates, payroll cut-offs and exceptions in pay calculations.

evidence.claim: Scenario costing can use deterministic calculations; package acceptability requires human judgement.
GDPR Article 22 matters if the design extends into solely automated decisions significantly affecting employees.
AI systems intended for specified worker evaluation or employment decisions may fall within Annex III.

assumptions: The specialist develops employer-side alternatives with support from compensation staff.
A spreadsheet commonly joins pay exports to bespoke bargaining assumptions.
The calculator compares aggregate packages and does not select individual employment outcomes.
The priors support substantial conversation and judgement; drafting gains do not replace these steps.
Build estimates include a pilot and applicable national consultation, but exclude procurement.
unknowns: Available pay data, data quality and authorised aggregation levels.
Existing costing models and which assumptions have been validated.
Whether union membership or other special-category data would be processed.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approval rights.
Which proposed benefits can be implemented in the current payroll configuration.
research_questions: Can existing calculation features cover the main proposal types?
How reliably do extracted changes preserve exceptions and eligibility conditions?
new_work: Validate scenario assumptions and reconcile calculation results.
Review drafted packages for feasibility and omitted employee groups.
Maintain pay rules and effective-date logic.
Reassess GDPR and EU AI Act obligations if the scope expands to individual decisions.
tasks.statement: Identify alternatives to proposals of unions, employees, companies, or government agencies.

tasks.short: Interpret collective agreements and explain their application to employers and employees.

steps.what: Clarify the question, affected workers and relevant dates.
Find applicable agreement versions, amendments and earlier interpretations.
Compare clauses and draft an interpretation with unresolved questions.

loop.input: Case scope and permission-filtered source pack with version identifiers.
loop.output: Interpretation draft with clause citations, alternatives and missing facts.
loop.check: Verify cited passages exist and match versions; specialist checks applicability and reasoning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved conflicts return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clause interactions and ambiguous language require contextual reading; keyword retrieval cannot settle them.

steps.what: Discuss competing readings and approve the advice within delegated authority.
Send approved advice and file the interpretation with its scope.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted case form in the {WORKFLOW} and index approved agreement versions in the {DOCS}. Deterministic retrieval supplies a source pack to a bounded drafting loop; the specialist approves the interpretation, recipients and release before the {EMAIL} sends it and the {DOCS} stores it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement versions, local amendments and earlier advice are scattered. Applicability often depends on facts absent from the request.
tasks.enabler_now: Version indexing and case forms are established technology. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded drafting can work from cited clauses.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting clauses, national rules and disputed facts still need specialist judgement. Earlier advice may be unsuitable for reuse.
tasks.human_edge: Explain ambiguity fairly, understand bargaining history and recognise when advice needs legal escalation.

ambition.what: An approved agreement interpretation clinic for frontline supervisors.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to searching and filing; more goes to difficult interpretations and supervisor advice. No additional authority to bind either party is implied.

reach.task: Answer routine questions about employment terms.
reach.learn: Agreement coverage, effective dates and thresholds for specialist escalation.

evidence.claim: Version retrieval, controlled drafting and approval routing are feasible building blocks; the digest provides no direct labor-relations implementation.
Generated interpretations need source checks and professional review; savings and accuracy require a local pilot.

assumptions: The company has collective agreements or comparable negotiated employment terms.
The specialist has delegated authority for routine advice and an escalation route for disputed interpretations.
Reusable templates can be portable; confidential employer records remain in an authorised workspace.
Build ranges cover a pilot with one agreement family and existing connectors, not waiting time for legal disputes.
unknowns: Which agreement versions and amendments are authoritative.
Whether earlier interpretations are approved, searchable and reusable.
The specialist's delegated authority and legal escalation route.
Available access, retention rules and consultation obligations under national rules.
research_questions: Can applicability be filtered reliably by worker group, location and effective date?
How often does a source-cited draft miss a relevant amendment or competing interpretation?
new_work: Maintain agreement versions and applicability metadata.
Review citations, ambiguity and recipients before release.
Withdraw superseded interpretations and handle retrieval failures.
Review GDPR safeguards and EU AI Act applicability for the actual intended use.
tasks.statement: Interpret contractual agreements for employers and employees engaged in collective bargaining or other labor relations processes.

tasks.short: Investigate union complaints, assess their merits and communicate a reasoned position.

steps.what: Register the complaint, acknowledge receipt and identify procedural deadlines.
Collect relevant employment records, agreements and correspondence.
Interview the complainant, manager and relevant witnesses.
Build a chronology and map allegations to evidence and agreement clauses.

loop.input: Access-approved evidence bundle, written interview notes and current agreement.
loop.output: Chronology and allegation-to-evidence matrix with source locations and contradictions.
loop.check: Validate source locations and dates; specialist checks completeness and disputed accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unreadable or contradictory material enters an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Accounts and allegations appear in varied free text rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Assess merits, procedural fairness and whether legal advice or further investigation is needed.
Draft the reasoned response and proposed next steps.

loop.input: Human case assessment, approved next steps and response template.
loop.output: Response draft explaining the assessment and procedural next steps.
loop.check: Match every finding to the approved assessment; flag unsupported legal statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing rationale returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual complaints require a tailored explanation beyond template fields.

steps.what: Approve and send the response through the agreed confidential channel.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted case queue in the {HELPDESK} and retrieve explicitly selected records from the {HCM}, {DOCS} and {EMAIL}. Bounded loops prepare a source-linked chronology and response draft; the specialist conducts interviews, determines the assessment and approves each external response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crosses restricted records and personal correspondence. Credibility, conflicting accounts and legal interpretation resist fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Case permissions, deadline rules and scoped retrieval can handle administration. Bounded extraction can organise free text without deciding complaint validity.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence may be incomplete, sensitive or contested. Union membership can be special-category data, and disclosure must protect other people's information.
tasks.human_edge: Hear people fairly, test competing accounts and make a defensible assessment without reducing credibility to a score.

ambition.what: Privacy-preserving grievance procedure improvement review.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconstructing files and more time on interviews and disputed facts. Case decision rights stay the same; aggregate findings can support recommendations for procedural improvements.

reach.task: Identify discrimination concerns that require a separate investigation route.
reach.learn: Referral thresholds, evidence preservation and protections against retaliation.

evidence.claim: Restricted case records, deadline tracking and evidence organisation are feasible supporting tools; the digest provides no direct labor-relations deployment case.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Dutch consultation and consent requirements can apply to employee-data arrangements; national rules elsewhere need separate assessment.

assumptions: A restricted case queue exists in the {HELPDESK}; otherwise configure an equivalent restricted record in the {WORKFLOW}.
Retrieval uses a human-selected case scope rather than searching all employee communications.
The tool produces no credibility score, employee ranking or automated complaint decision.
Time shares are estimates; interviews and judgment remain substantial despite document automation.
Access work includes GDPR lawful-basis and special-category conditions, retention, EU AI Act intended-use assessment, and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Which grievance deadlines and escalation procedures apply?
Which records may investigators access and disclose?
Who must approve responses in serious or legally contested cases?
Which consultation, privacy assessment and employee-information steps are required?
research_questions: Does the existing case system enforce case-specific access and disclosure controls?
Can extraction preserve contradictory accounts and identify missing evidence on representative closed cases?
new_work: Verify chronology entries, evidence links and omitted material.
Handle missing records and access exceptions.
Maintain procedure deadlines, response templates and retention rules.
Review access logs and prevent identifiable small-group reporting.
tasks.statement: Investigate and evaluate union complaints or arguments to determine viability.

tasks.short: Mediate between employer and employee representatives to reconcile differences.

steps.what: Arrange participation, availability and confidentiality expectations.
Read each party's submission and prepare a neutral agenda.
Facilitate discussion, explore interests and test possible resolutions.
Record proposed terms and obtain each party's explicit agreement.
Record agreed actions, send reminders and arrange follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling and approved reminders through the {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. A deterministic agenda and resolution generator in the {DOCS} uses structured fields entered by the specialist, with separate access for private notes and shared terms. Parties approve the resolution, and the specialist approves action owners, recipients and reminders before follow-up begins.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most value comes from a trusted conversation. Small administrative savings were fragmented across scheduling, notes and follow-up.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, templates and reminders can cover the administrative work. A small amount of integration makes them usable together without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Power imbalances, trust, confidential disclosures and willingness to compromise remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what parties mean, manage tension and recognise whether agreement is informed and voluntary.
tasks.altitude: Most of the week still involves preparation and mediation. Administrative effort falls modestly; settlement authority remains with the parties.

reach.task: Follow through on actions agreed during mediation.
reach.learn: Confidentiality boundaries, voluntary agreement and escalation when commitments fail.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, structured document generation and reminders can support mediation without automating the conversation.
The digest provides no direct mediation automation case; substantial time savings are not established.

assumptions: The specialist acts as an accepted facilitator within the company's process.
The parties retain authority to accept or reject proposed terms.
Preparation uses structured templates; reading sensitive submissions remains human.
The solution does not record or analyse the mediation conversation.
unknowns: Whether the specialist is sufficiently independent for the proposed mediation.
Which notes can be retained or shared under national rules and participation terms.
How each party confirms agreement and who can commit the employer.
Whether consultation is required for the proposed recordkeeping changes.
research_questions: Which administrative steps actually delay mediation in representative cases?
Can existing access controls keep private preparation notes separate from shared resolutions?
new_work: Maintain neutral templates and participation terms.
Check shared recipients and keep private notes restricted.
Handle declined appointments and failed reminders.
Check completion of agreed actions without exposing confidential discussion.
tasks.statement: Mediate discussions between employer and employee representatives in attempt to reconcile differences.

tasks.short: Check adherence to labor agreements and resolve potential departures.

steps.what: Translate agreement clauses into checks, evidence requirements and review dates.

loop.input: Current agreement and approved interpretations.
loop.output: Proposed checklist with clauses, effective dates, evidence and ambiguous obligations.
loop.check: Specialist approves every interpretation and executable rule before activation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous clauses remain manual checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreements express obligations in varied prose; literal matching misses qualifications.

steps.what: Retrieve pay, hours, absence and staffing evidence for the review period.
Compare recorded practice against measurable agreement requirements.
Investigate exceptions and obligations that require contextual interpretation.
Discuss findings and disputed interpretations with managers and workforce representatives.
Approve corrective actions or escalate unresolved interpretations.
Update the action register and remind responsible teams about deadlines.

tasks.design: A reviewed control checklist in {DOCS} drives scheduled checks on permitted {HCM} and {PAYROLL} data through {DATA_PLATFORM}. A restricted {WORKFLOW} register holds evidence, exceptions and approved remediation, with internal reminders and a status view. People investigate context, discuss contested findings and approve corrective actions before affected teams execute them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement clauses were not executable rules, and evidence crossed records, documents and local interpretations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and workflow features can support routine controls. AI coding reduces the effort of joining records and building checks; a bounded model only proposes clause extraction.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive changes, local exceptions and ambiguous entitlements need careful interpretation. A detected mismatch is not proof of misconduct or non-compliance.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing administrative errors from substantive breaches and resolving disputed interpretations fairly.

ambition.what: Review emerging agreement exceptions each pay cycle.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconciling records and more time resolving exceptions before they recur. They can prioritise investigations; disciplinary and pay decisions retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Trace and correct an agreement-related pay discrepancy.
reach.learn: Pay codes, retrospective adjustments, effective dates and payroll cut-offs.

evidence.claim: Deterministic controls can compare structured records with approved agreement rules; no direct implementation case is supplied.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
The Dutch supervisory list identifies employee-monitoring processing requiring a DPIA.
The EU AI Act identifies specified employment and worker-management AI uses as high-risk.

assumptions: Existing system records contain enough evidence for a useful subset of agreement checks.
Checks flag discrepancies and missing evidence; they do not score worker conduct or determine entitlements.
Document review and discussion remain substantial, while measurable reconciliation supports more automation than the overall task prior suggests.
Build ranges include a pilot across historical pay periods.
unknowns: Which obligations are measurable from existing records.
Whether time records are available through the {HCM} or require another source.
The quality of effective dates, worker categories and local exceptions.
Existing GDPR assessments, access restrictions and national consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which checks reproduce confirmed historical discrepancies without excessive false alarms?
Does the proposed use constitute employee monitoring or high-risk worker-management AI?
Which controls can be configured in existing systems before custom code is needed?
new_work: Approve and version control rules when agreements change.
Investigate false positives and missing evidence.
Reconcile source totals and monitor integration failures.
Review access, retention and the continued necessity of each data field.
tasks.statement: Monitor company or workforce adherence to labor agreements.

tasks.short: Negotiate collective agreements within an approved mandate and secure valid agreement.

steps.what: Assemble proposals, cost scenarios and outstanding issues into a bargaining pack.
Agree negotiating limits, concessions and escalation points.
Bargain with employee representatives and test concessions within the mandate.
Write the session record and consolidate tentative terms.

loop.input: Written negotiation notes and expressly recorded tentative terms.
loop.output: Source-linked session record and settlement draft with unresolved wording marked.
loop.check: Specialist checks every commitment against notes; conflicting accounts remain unresolved.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or disputed terms return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need synthesis; templates alone cannot distinguish discussion from agreement.

steps.what: Check settlement wording against applicable law and existing agreements.
Approve settlement terms or return outstanding issues to negotiation.
Complete required ratification, signatures and agreement filing.

tasks.design: A controlled pack generator assembles approved material from the {DOCS}, {CLM} and {SPREADSHEET}; a bounded drafting loop prepares session records from written notes. Configure the {WORKFLOW} and {ESIGN} for settlement approvals and signatures, while people retain bargaining, legal review and ratification.
tasks.previous_blocker: The central work depends on trust, mandates and concessions. Supporting documents have separate owners and changing versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and signature features handle routing. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building pack assembly and document checks; bounded drafting can reduce note preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing terms remains slow and political. Sector agreements, national rules and representative ratification can constrain local authority.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, preserve trust and judge when a concession creates a workable agreement.

ambition.what: Joint implementation readiness review before an agreement takes effect.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling packs and recording meetings; bargaining remains most of the work. The specialist can coordinate implementation readiness, but gains no additional settlement authority.
